```{r setup, include=FALSE}
# Number the exported plots in the order they appear: 01-..., 02-...
fig_counter <- 0
number_figures <- function(path) {
  fig_counter <<- fig_counter + 1
  new_path <- file.path(dirname(path), sprintf("%02d-%s", fig_counter, basename(path)))
  file.rename(path, new_path)
  new_path
}

knitr::opts_chunk$set(
  echo       = TRUE,
  collapse   = TRUE,
  comment    = "#>",
  warning    = FALSE,
  message    = FALSE,
  fig.path   = "output/",
  fig.width  = 9,
  fig.height = 5.5,
  dpi        = 150,
  out.width  = "100%",
  fig.process = number_figures
)
```

# Analysis

## 1. Libraries and Data

Load the packages and import the tablet weight data.

```{r libraries}
library(qcc)
library(ggplot2)
library(dplyr)
library(forecast)
library(moments)
```

```{r import-data}
tablet_weight <- read.csv("data/tablet_weight.csv")

# Check the data
head(tablet_weight)
tail(tablet_weight)
```

## 2. Data Audit

Check the structure of the data and look for missing values.

```{r data-audit}
# Basic Data Audit
glimpse(tablet_weight)

cat("Dimensions (rows, columns):", dim(tablet_weight), "\n")

if (anyNA(tablet_weight)) {
  cat("⚠ Missing values detected in the dataset.\n")
} else {
  cat("✓ No missing values. Summary:\n\n")
  data.frame(
    col    = names(tablet_weight),
    type   = sapply(tablet_weight, class),
    unique = sapply(tablet_weight, \(x) length(unique(x)))
  )
}
```

Remove the index column `X` and rename the variables.

```{r clean-data}
# Get rid of X column and change the column names
tablet_weight <- tablet_weight |>
  select(-X) |>
  rename(
    target_value = Weight.target.value,
    weight_value = Weight.value
  )

glimpse(tablet_weight)
```

## 3. Phase I and Phase II

The first 100 observations (Phase I) calibrate the control limits. The remaining 37 (Phase II) are used for monitoring.

```{r phases}
weight_value <- tablet_weight$weight_value
phase1 <- weight_value[1:100]
phase2 <- weight_value[101:length(weight_value)]

cat("Phase I (n):", length(phase1), "| Phase II (n):", length(phase2), "\n")
```

## 4. I-MR Control Chart

Many points fall beyond the limits or form violating runs, so the process is not behaving as a stable, independent process.

```{r imr-chart, fig.height=6.5}
# Run Shewhart I-MR Chart
par(mar = c(9, 4, 4, 2))
imr <- qcc(
  data = phase1,
  newdata = phase2,
  type = "xbar.one",
  title = "Tablet Weight - I-MR Chart",
  xlab = "Observation",
  ylab = "Weight (mg)",
  add.stats = TRUE
)

summary(imr)
```

Summary of the violations detected by the chart:

```{r imr-violations}
imr_beyond_limits <- imr$violations$beyond.limits
imr_violation_runs <- imr$violations$violating.runs

imr_violations <- data.frame(
  Type  = c("Beyond limits", "Violating runs", "Total (unique)"),
  Count = c(length(imr_beyond_limits),
            length(imr_violation_runs),
            length(unique(c(imr_beyond_limits,
                            imr_violation_runs))))
)
cat("I-MR Chart — Violations Summary\n\n")
imr_violations
```

## 5. Graphical Data Exploration

Distribution of the tablet weight values.

```{r histogram}
# Histogram of Tablet Weight Values
optimal_bins <- round(1 + log(length(phase1), base = 2))
ggplot() +
  aes(x = phase1) +
  geom_histogram(bins = optimal_bins, fill = "steelblue", color = "black") +
  geom_density(fill = "blue", alpha = 0.5) +
  geom_vline(aes(xintercept = mean(weight_value),
                 color = "Mean"),
             linetype = "dashed", linewidth = 1) +
  geom_vline(aes(xintercept = median(weight_value),
                 color = "Median"),
             linetype = "dashed", linewidth = 1) +
  scale_color_manual(name   = NULL,
                     values = c("Mean"   = "red",
                                "Median" = "darkgreen")) +
  labs(title = "Distribution of Tablet Weight",
       x = "Weight (mg)", y = "Count") +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(legend.position = "right")
```

Boxplot and outlier detection.

```{r boxplot, fig.height=4}
# Box-plot of Tablet Weight Values
ggplot() +
  aes(x = phase1) +
  geom_boxplot(fill = "steelblue", outlier.color = "red", outlier.size = 2) +
  labs(title = "Tablet Weight — Boxplot", x = "Weight (mg)") +
  theme_minimal()
```

```{r outliers}
out_vals <- boxplot.stats(weight_value)$out
out_pos <- which(weight_value %in% out_vals)

data.frame(
  n_outliers = length(out_vals),
  Positions  = paste(out_pos, collapse = ", "),
  Values     = paste(round(out_vals, 2), collapse = ", "),
  Skewness   = round(skewness(phase1), 2)
)
```

As we can observe at the histogram and box-plot graphs, there are hints the data doesn't follow a normal distribution.

## 6. Autocorrelation Diagnosis

A slowly decaying ACF indicates that consecutive observations are correlated, which violates the independence assumption of the Shewhart chart, causing many false alarms.

```{r acf-raw}
acf(phase1,
    lag.max = 20,
    type     = "correlation",
    plot     = TRUE,
    main = "ACF Plot of Tablet Weight"
    )
```

Ljung-Box test (H0: no autocorrelation).

```{r ljung-raw}
Box.test(phase1, lag = 20, type = "Ljung-Box")
```

We reject H0 given a significant level of 0.05, therefore, there is enough evidence tablet weight data has autocorrelation.

## 7. Normality Diagnosis

Q-Q plot and Shapiro-Wilk test (H0: normality).

```{r qq-raw}
ggplot() +
  aes(sample = phase1) +
  stat_qq() +
  stat_qq_line(color = "red") +
  labs(title = "Q-Q Plot — Phase 1 Tablet Weight",
       x = "Theoretical Quantiles",
       y = "Sample Quantiles (mg)") +
  theme_minimal()
```

Shapiro-Wilk test (H0: normal data).

```{r shapiro-raw}
shapiro.test(phase1)
```

We reject H0 given a significant level of 0.05, therefore, there is enough evidence tablet weight data doesn't follow a normal distribution.

## 8. ARIMA Model

An ARIMA model is fitted to Phase I to remove the autocorrelation.

```{r arima}
# ARIMA Model
arima_model <- auto.arima(phase1)
arimaorder(arima_model)
residuals <- as.numeric(arima_model$residuals)
```

Residual diagnostics: autocorrelation (ACF and Ljung-Box).

```{r acf-residuals}
# ACF Plot for ARIMA Residuals
acf(residuals,
    lag.max = 20,
    type     = "correlation",
    plot     = TRUE,
    main = "ACF Plot of Residuals of ARIMA Model"
    )
```

```{r ljung-residuals}
Box.test(residuals, lag = 20, type = "Ljung-Box")
```

We fail to reject H0 given a significant level of 0.05, therefore, there is enough evidence ARIMA residuals doesn't have autocorrelation.

Residual diagnostics: normality (Q-Q plot and Shapiro-Wilk).

```{r qq-residuals}
# Normality Test for ARIMA Residuals
ggplot() +
  aes(sample = residuals) +
  stat_qq() +
  stat_qq_line(color = "red") +
  labs(title = "Q-Q Plot — Residuals of ARIMA Model",
       x = "Theoretical Quantiles",
       y = "Sample Quantiles") +
  theme_minimal()
```

```{r shapiro-residuals}
shapiro.test(residuals)
```

We reject H0 given a significant level of 0.05, therefore, there is enough evidence tablet ARIMA residuals doesn't follow a normal distribution.

## 9. EWMA Chart

The EWMA chart of the residuals is robust to non-normal data. Points beyond the limits (red) indicate special causes.

```{r ewma, fig.height=6.5}
# EWMA Plot
ewma_chart <- ewma(residuals,
                   lambda     = 0.1,
                   nsigmas    = 2.7,
                   add.stats = TRUE,
                   xlab = "Observation",
                   ylab = "Exponentially Weighted Residual"
                   )

summary(ewma_chart)
```

### EWMA Chart After Removing the Outlier

The ARIMA model and the EWMA chart are repeated without the outlier. Removing it is only valid if a special cause is identified and justified with the 6M analysis (manpower, machines, materials, methods, measurement and mother nature). The first ARIMA/EWMA (`ewma_chart`) is kept to classify the process.

```{r ewma-clean, fig.height=6.5}
# EWMA Chart After Removing the Outlier
new_arima_model <- auto.arima(phase1[-out_pos])
arimaorder(new_arima_model)
new_residuals <- as.numeric(new_arima_model$residuals)
ewma_chart_clean <- ewma(new_residuals,
                         lambda     = 0.1,
                         nsigmas    = 2.7,
                         add.stats = TRUE,
                         xlab = "Observation",
                         ylab = "Exponentially Weighted Residual"
                         )
```

After removing the outlier, previous out-of-control points of EWMA chart fell between the limits, correcting the instability of the process.

## 10. Process Capability

Capability indices against the specification limits (target ± 10 %).

```{r capability, fig.height=6}
# Capability Analysis
target <- unique(tablet_weight$target_value)
lsl <- target*(1-0.10)
usl <- target*(1+0.10)
capability <- process.capability(imr, spec.limits = c(lsl, usl))
capability$indices
```

## 11. Process Classification

Stability comes from the first EWMA chart and capability from Cp and Cpk (threshold = 1.33).

```{r classification}
# Process Classification
stable <- length(ewma_chart$violations) == 0

threshold <- 1.33
capable <- all(capability$indices[c("Cp", "Cp_k"), "Value"] >= threshold)

type <- if (stable && capable) "A" else
  if (!stable && capable) "B" else
    if (stable && !capable) "C" else "D"

# Type of Process
descriptions <- c(
  A = "Stable and capable — ideal process.",
  B = "Capable but unstable — meets specifications but unpredictable.",
  C = "Stable but incapable — predictable but produces nonconforming units.",
  D = "Unstable and incapable — worst state."
)

cat("Type:", type, "\n")
cat("Summary:", descriptions[type], "\n")
```

Classification when the Taguchi index (Cpm) is also required to meet the threshold:

```{r classification-cpm}
capable_cpm <- all(capability$indices[c("Cp", "Cp_k", "Cpm"), "Value"] >= threshold)

type_cpm <- if (stable && capable_cpm) "A" else
  if (!stable && capable_cpm) "B" else
    if (stable && !capable_cpm) "C" else "D"

cat("Type (including Cpm):", type_cpm, "\n")
cat("Summary:", descriptions[type_cpm], "\n")
```

# Summary of Results

- **Stability:** the EWMA chart shows `r length(ewma_chart$violations)` points beyond limits, so the process is **`r if (stable) "stable" else "unstable"`**.
- **Capability:** Cp = `r format(round(capability$indices["Cp", "Value"], 4), nsmall = 4)` and Cpk = `r format(round(capability$indices["Cp_k", "Value"], 4), nsmall = 4)`.
- **Classification: Type `r type`.** `r descriptions[type]`
- **Important:** taking Cpm (Taguchi index = `r format(round(capability$indices["Cpm", "Value"], 3), nsmall = 3)`) into account, the process is **Type `r type_cpm`**. `r descriptions[type_cpm]`

# Function Overview

The project defines no custom functions. It consists of two scripts that rely on the following package functions.

| Script | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `sqc_analysis.R` | Data audit, Phase I/II split, control charts, diagnostics, ARIMA, EWMA, capability and process classification |
| `plot_generator.R` | Reproduces every plot and saves it to `output/` |

| Function | Package | Use |
|---|---|---|
| `qcc()` | qcc | I-MR (individuals) control chart |
| `ewma()` | qcc | EWMA chart on ARIMA residuals |
| `process.capability()` | qcc | Cp, Cpk and Cpm indices |
| `auto.arima()` | forecast | Autocorrelation correction |
| `skewness()` | moments | Distribution shape |
| `acf()`, `Box.test()`, `shapiro.test()` | stats | Autocorrelation and normality diagnostics |
| `ggplot()` | ggplot2 | Histogram, boxplot, Q-Q plots |
